{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

Rule order in sm_github.json: merge-validated (147) → fail-validation (161) → sweep-stale-validating (179) → silent-update-behind → park-reset → validate-armed (246) → ... So the sweep runs before validate-armed. 

Now, the design, concretely:

### New module: `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

Pure functions, GraalJS-safe, CommonJS — mirrors `reworkLatch.js` style. Contents:

1. **Liveness classification** — `classifyRun({active, newest}, opts)`:
   - `probe.newest` = the newest dispatched run on the head (any status), `probe.active` = hasActiveDispatchedRun semantics (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending, or completed within the 15-min visibility grace).
   - Returns:
     - `'running'` — active run (in-flight, or a conclusion inside the check-visibility grace — NOT yet a zombie; this preserves the race windows)
     - `'green'` — newest concluded success (verdict path — sweep success side, unchanged)
     - `'red'` — newest concluded failure/timed_out (verdict path — sweep fail side, unchanged)
     - `'zombie-cancelled'` — newest run concluded cancelled (and past the visibility grace)
     - `'zombie-no-run'` — no dispatched run on the head at all
     - null — newest unreadable (probe failure → fail CLOSED: treat as running? The sweep probe "must FAIL CLOSED (null): an unwarranted unarm tears a live arm" — for the zombie branch, a null newest must NOT classify as zombie → return null → arm stays.)

2. **Zombie re-dispatch tracker** (marker-comment based, same carrier as red-head markers):
   - `ZOMBIE_MARKER_RE` — parses `🔄 zombie re-dispatch N/3 — head <sha> (7+) at <iso>` hmm, let me design the marker line format:
     `🔄 zombie re-dispatch #N for head <sha> at <iso> (zombie re-dispatch 1/hour, 3 = validation_failed park)` — the regex needs (sha, N, iso). Let me follow the red-head style: `🔄 zombie re-dispatch <sha> — zombie <N> at <iso>`. Regex: /🔄 zombie re-dispatch ([0-9a-f]{7,40}) — zombie (\d+) at ([0-9T:\.\-Z]+)/g
   - `zombieState(comments, headSha)` → { count, lastAtMs } — scans marker comments for the head; count = max N recorded for this head; lastAtMs = newest marker timestamp for this head.
   - `zombieMarkerLine(priorCount, headSha, cap)` → the next marker line (N = prior + 1).
   - `zombieCapOf(jobParams)` → default 3.
   - `zombieRedispatchMinMs(jobParams)` → default 1h.
   
   Hmm wait — should this live in the common module or in smAgent.js? The red-head/empty-lap markers live in smAgent.js (module scope) with `failMarkerState`. The zombie tracker is a distinct concern; the ticket describes it as a "liveness state machine". For testability, a pure module `js/common/validationLiveness.js` with classification + marker math, wired in smAgent.js (comment reads via `github_get_pr_comments` like failMarkerState). Tests: `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` (pure) + extend `test_smAgent.js` for the sweep handler wiring. This mirrors how reworkLatch was added (common module + smAgent wiring + test_smAgent coverage + maybe its own test file).

### Sweep handler changes (`sweep_stale_validation` in smAgent.js)

Current:
```js
var sProbe = sHead ? probeDispatchedState(effectiveRepoInfo, sCiWf, sHead) : null;
var sRun = sProbe ? sProbe.newest : null;
var sOld = false;
if (sRun && sRun.status === 'completed' && sRun.conclusion && sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled') {
    var sDone = Date.parse(sRun.updated_at || sRun.created_at || '');
    sOld = !isNaN(sDone) && (Date.now() - sDone) > sStaleMin * 60 * 1000;
}
if (!sOld) {
    console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays');
    continue;
}
if (sRun.conclusion === 'success') { ...latch... continue; }
sweepFailure = true; // fail path
```

New flow:
```js
var sProbe = sHead ? probeDispatchedState(...) : null;
var sState = validationLivenessModule.classify(sProbe, {...});  // running/green/red/zombie-cancelled/zombie-no-run/null
if (sState === 'zombie-cancelled' || sState === 'zombie-no-run') → zombie branch
else → existing logic (unchanged shapes + log lines preserved)
```

Careful: the existing `!sOld` case covers BOTH "no run" and "fresh conclusion" AND "cancelled conclusion" — all currently log "no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays". Existing unit tests assert that message for cancelled (test_smAgent.js:3002). The zombie branch REPLACES that for cancelled/no-run — so those tests will need updating (the bug fix changes exactly that behavior — that's expected: the previous behavior IS the bug). But careful about "no run": currently "no run" → arm stays. New: "no run" → zombie → re-dispatch. Hmm — is that safe for the latch-skip arm (arm WITHOUT dispatch)? Latch-skip arms carry a GREEN run on the head (the latch requires vProbe.green) → newest = green → not zombie. Safe. What about an arm whose dispatch landed seconds ago (run not yet registered)? `probe.active` — hasActiveDispatchedRun returns false (no runs found) → newest = null → 'zombie-no-run'! DANGER: the fresh arm races the run registration. The gh-748 guard exists exactly for this: registration lag seconds after `gh workflow run` returns. The sweep runs at most ~0-10 min after the arm (validate-armed runs AFTER the sweep in the same tick — arm at T, sweep sees it at T+10min... hmm actually within one tick, sweep runs BEFORE validate-armed, so a PR armed THIS tick gets swept NEXT tick — 10 min later — registration long done). But other arm sites: validate_pr arms happen in validate-armed/revalidate-armed/validate-fresh — all AFTER the sweep in rule order... EXCEPT revalidate-armed-green? No — also after (#311). All validate_pr rules are after sweep-stale-validating (#179)? validate-armed #246, revalidate-armed #279, revalidate-armed-green #311, validate-fresh #334, validate-fresh-masked-green #359. Yes — all after. So a PR armed in tick N is first swept in tick N+1 (≥10 min later). Registration lag (seconds) long gone.

BUT: manual arms (human adds the label by hand) could hit the sweep immediately. And the arm-then-sweep ordering could interleave differently in machine-sm vs machine_merge? The sweep rule exists in sm_github.json — machine-sm. For safety, the zombie-no-run branch must ALSO check the gh-748-style recent-run guard (`hasRecentHeadRun(headWorkflowRunsSafe(...), grace)`) — any run (any workflow, any event) active or completed within the dispatch-race grace (60s default) → not a zombie, arm stays. That covers a JUST-dispatched run registered under any event. But 60s grace doesn't cover a manual arm 5 min ago whose dispatch is registering — that's beyond realistic registration lag; fine.

Hmm — also what about the arm that just fired its dispatch but the run takes a while to QUEue...? workflow_dispatch runs appear in the API within seconds (the gh-748 lag is seconds). OK.

Additionally: for the no-run zombie, require... hmm, what about `stampValidationChecksForModule`-stamped repos (bridge-free)? The stamped check runs are bookkeeping-ignored? No — the stamps are the validationChecks names, real contexts. They'd fold into the rollup, not the dispatched-run probe. The dispatched-run probe only looks at workflow_dispatch runs of ciWorkflow. A stamped repo that failed to dispatch → no dispatched runs → zombie-no-run → re-dispatch. Good — that's the lost-dispatch dead-zone case, which revalidate-armed (checks none) also covers, but when the stamped in_progress check run makes the rollup read 'pending' and the PR is NOT approved (dev lane)... revalidate-armed requires pr_approved. validate-fresh requires NOT ai_validating. So an armed dev-lane PR with a lost dispatch = dead zone today → zombie fixe…

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).

          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is

        run: |

Now, the design, concretely:

### New module: `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

Pure functions, GraalJS-safe, CommonJS — mirrors `reworkLatch.js` style. Contents:

1. **Liveness classification** — `classifyRun({active, newest}, opts)`:
   - `probe.newest` = the newest dispatched run on the head (any status), `probe.active` = hasActiveDispatchedRun semantics (queued/in_progress/waiting/pending, or completed within the 15-min visibility grace).
   - Returns:
     - `'running'` — active run (in-flight, or a conclusion inside the check-visibility grace — NOT yet a zombie; this preserves the race windows)
     - `'green'` — newest concluded success (verdict path — sweep success side, unchanged)
     - `'red'` — newest concluded failure/timed_out (verdict path — sweep fail side, unchanged)
     - `'zombie-cancelled'` — newest run concluded cancelled (and past the visibility grace)
     - `'zombie-no-run'` — no dispatched run on the head at all
     - null — newest unreadable (probe failure → fail CLOSED: treat as running? The sweep probe "must FAIL CLOSED (null): an unwarranted unarm tears a live arm" — for the zombie branch, a null newest must NOT classify as zombie → return null → arm stays.)

2. **Zombie re-dispatch tracker** (marker-comment based, same carrier as red-head markers):

Let me follow the red-head style: `🔄 zombie re-dispatch <sha> — zombie <N> at <iso>`. Regex: /🔄 zombie re-dispatch ([0-9a-f]{7,40}) — zombie (\d+) at ([0-9T:\.\-Z]+)/g
   - `zombieState(comments, headSha)` → { count, lastAtMs } — scans marker comments for the head; count = max N recorded for this head; lastAtMs = newest marker timestamp for this head.
   - `zombieMarkerLine(priorCount, headSha, cap)` → the next marker line (N = prior + 1).
   - `zombieCapOf(jobParams)` → default 3.
   - `zombieRedispatchMinMs(jobParams)` → default 1h.

The zombie tracker is a distinct concern; the ticket describes it as a "liveness state machine". {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure).       - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner

        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).
"}

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).

A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. {"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost entirely) holds the serial `ai_validating` mutex forever — the merge window starves until a human manually re-dispatches CI.

**Root cause**: `sweep_stale_validation` in `js/smAgent.js` (stale-arm sweeper, ~line 2645) only sweeps arms whose dispatched run concluded a VERDICT: `sRun.conclusion !== 'cancelled'` gates the stale computation, so a cancelled-only head (or a head with no dispatched run at all) falls into the `!sOld` branch — `⏭️ sweep: no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays` — and loops forever. `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755/#682) is correct for verdict *consumption*, but the sweeper also uses it as the excuse to never *re-drive* the run. With the arm stuck on PR #1443, `validate-armed`'s query-time mutex scan (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`, `q.mutex` + `mutexAmong: [pr_approved]`) deferred every other approved candidate each tick (`🔒 mutex ai_validating held`).

**Impact**: Any single cancelled/lost dispatch on an armed head freezes its validation slot — and for an approved arm the whole merge window — indefinitely. Live incident (dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09): fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`, its dispatched run concluded cancelled 13:36Z (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 family), four validated PRs deferred, merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing liveness states to the sweep (gh-821 capability surface):
- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): classify the head's dispatched-run probe into `running` / `green` / `red` / `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`. `probe.active` (existing `hasActiveDispatchedRun` semantics: in-flight, or concluded within the 15-min check-visibility grace) keeps all race windows intact — a fresh cancellation still reads `running`.
- Sweep zombie branch (smAgent): zombie ⇒ same-tick re-dispatch (release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the head, re-arm — the re-dispatch re-acquires the mutex with a LIVE run behind it; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`). Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour, bookkept with a marker comment per re-dispatch (same carrier as the red-head markers — durable, zero extra infrastructure). Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, #633/gh-750 reset semantics recover it on a new head).
- AC3 (healthy flow) is untouched: a live run keeps the arm exactly as today; green/red conclusions keep the existing verdict paths verbatim.

**Non-goals honored**: no parallel validations (the re-dispatch re-acquires the serial slot within the same action), no change to the gh-748 race guard itself (the zombie branch composes with it via the `hasRecentHeadRun` belt check).

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest).       - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest).
