One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})

          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

messages.preview: The failure is a test-expectation question: `classify({})` (truthy probe, no facets) → `zombie-no-run` is the deliberate gh-821 bias (a wedged arm is worse than one bounded duplicate dispatch). Fix th…

blocks.text:
One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. Actually — cleaner: drop the `{}` case from the "fail safe to running" test and assert it as zombie-no-run explicitly (documenting the deliberate choice), keeping `null` → running.

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). blocks.text:
One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). messages.preview: The failure is a test-expectation question: `classify({})` (truthy probe, no facets) → `zombie-no-run` is the deliberate gh-821 bias (a wedged arm is worse than one bounded duplicate dispatch). Fix th…

blocks.text:
One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. Actually — cleaner: drop the `{}` case from the "fail safe to running" test and assert it as zombie-no-run explicitly (documenting the deliberate choice), keeping `null` → running.

blocks.text:
One failure: `classify({})` — my test expected 'running' for a completely empty probe object, but classify returns 'zombie-no-run' because `probe.active` is undefined (not true) and newest is null. 

Which is right? Design intent: a probe BUNDLE that exists but has no facets — in smAgent, `probeDispatchedState` always returns all 4 facets (active/verdict/green/newest). `{ active: false, newest: null }` IS the zombie-no-run shape (probe ran, no runs found). The pure `{}` case is a malformed probe. My test assertion `classify({}) === 'running'` was overly defensive; but the doc says "degraded shapes fail safe" — hmm. What's the safest semantic?

- `classify(null)` → 'running' (no probe at all — the smAgent sweep passes null when sHead is null; the existing behavior for null probe is arm-stays). ✓ keep.
- `classify({})` — ambiguous. The realistic degraded case in smAgent is `sProbe = null` (no head) or a failed probe → `{active:false, newest:null}` (all helpers fail closed individually). A truly empty object never occurs from probeDispatchedState. Both semantics are defensible; the question is which is safer. `zombie-no-run` on a malformed probe → re-dispatch bounded 1/hour (fail-open toward recovery). `running` → arm stays (fail-safe toward stillness — the pre-fix deadlock behavior).

Given the whole POINT of gh-821 is that a wedged arm is the worse failure mode, and the rate bound caps any wrongful churn, I'll treat a truthy probe object with missing facets as zombie-no-run (consistent: active!==true && !newest). Update the TEST (not the module): `classify({})` → 'zombie-no-run'. The test comment should explain. Actually — cleaner: drop the `{}` case from the "fail safe to running" test and assert it as zombie-no-run explicitly (documenting the deliberate choice), keeping `null` → running.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

- Probe-error degeneracy is deliberate: `newestDispatchedRun` fails closed (null), so a degraded read classifies `zombie-no-run` — worst case one bounded duplicate CI run (1/head/hour), never a wedge; a wrongful `running` classification would re-create the deadlock.
- The zombie branch composes with gh-748 (belt check: any run on the head active or completed within the dispatch-race grace keeps the arm) and leaves gh-755 / rerun-cancelled-checks untouched — fresh cancellations still read `running` for their first 15 minutes.
- AC4 (live fa verification on the next cancelled run) is owner-verified; expected recovery ≤ 2 ticks (~15-min visibility grace + one 10-min cadence) instead of a manual unstick.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

- Probe-error degeneracy is deliberate: `newestDispatchedRun` fails closed (null), so a degraded read classifies `zombie-no-run` — worst case one bounded duplicate CI run (1/head/hour), never a wedge; a wrongful `running` classification would re-create the deadlock.
- The zombie branch composes with gh-748 (belt check: any run on the head active or completed within the dispatch-race grace keeps the arm) and leaves gh-755 / rerun-cancelled-checks untouched — fresh cancellations still read `running` for their first 15 minutes.
- AC4 (live fa verification on the next cancelled run) is owner-verified; expected recovery ≤ 2 ticks (~15-min visibility grace + one 10-min cadence) instead of a manual unstick.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

- Probe-error degeneracy is deliberate: `newestDispatchedRun` fails closed (null), so a degraded read classifies `zombie-no-run` — worst case one bounded duplicate CI run (1/head/hour), never a wedge; a wrongful `running` classification would re-create the deadlock.

{"content":"### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).

- **`js/common/validationLiveness.js`** (new, pure): liveness state machine — `running` (in-flight or inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, preserving the gh-748/gh-755 race windows), `green`/`red` (verdict paths unchanged), `zombie-cancelled`/`zombie-no-run`; plus marker-comment bookkeeping math (per-head crash-loop cap, hourly rate bound).

Bounded 1 re-dispatch per head per hour; 3 in a row on one head ⇒ `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, recovered by a new head SHA via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). AC3: live runs keep the arm exactly as today.
- **`sm_github.json`**: sweep rule description documents the amendment and the new knobs.

**Verification**: 24 new unit tests (16 pure-module L1 liveness cases + 8 smAgent sweep cases); the three new behaviors confirmed **RED on the pre-fix engine** (baseline `58a2dbf`, suite green there) and **GREEN after**; full suite `run_all.json` **2204 passed, 0 failed** — no regressions.
